This petition filed under Section 397 r/w Section 401 Cr.P.C, is by the accused challenging the impugned order by which the trial Court dismissed the application filed by him under Section 227 Cr.P.C seeking discharge.
2. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to by their ranks before the trial Court.
3. On 10.01.2023, a complaint came to be filed by the prosecutrix alleging
that she is resident of Chattisgarh
. Through Linked she was offered a job in Raj Builder India Private Limited.
She was suppose to report on 10.01.2023.

After traveling 28 hours, she reached Yeshwanthpur NC:
2025:KHC:15193 Railway Station on 09.01.2023 at 7.30 p.m.
She was informed by the Kashish of HR of the company that she would be picked up by a driver of the company.
However, accused claiming to be the Managing Director came to receive her in his black Jaguar car.
On the way, he explained the rules and regulations and informed her that except the company employees no one is allowed in the guest house.
She was also not allowed to bring her sisters and relatives.
3.1 At 8.30 p.m, they reached the guest house situated at Sanjayanagar.
Accused directed her to freshen up and he would take her to dinner and left the guest house for one hour.

After 20 minutes,
someone rang the bell and introduced himself as the owner of the said house.
Complainant showed him her Aadhar card.
In the meanwhile, Himanshi, a friend of complainant who is studying in Ramaiah Law College came to meet her.
When she informed accused over phone that her friend has come to meet her, he objected.
She convinced accused that as NC: 2025:KHC:15193 she is feeling uncomfortable, he should allow her friend to join dinner.
However, accused insisted them to having dinner outside the company and took parcel and dropped Himanshi.
3.2 Complainant and accused went back to the guest house at 12.00 a.m.
Accused insisted that he would come inside the guest house under the pretext of explaining the rules and regulations of company and allow him to have dinner inside the guest house.
When complainant went inside the room to get attested copies of her marks sheet, accused pounced on her from behind.
He held her waist and hugged tightly, forcibly pushed her on the bed and smooched her repeatedly.
He started pressing her breast and other private part forcefully and tried to insert his penis into her vagina.
Complainant was completely shocked and stunned while accused repeatedly kissed her with open jacket and shirt.
He kissed on her neck and attempted to remove her clothes.

sentences.text: Somehow, she gathered strength and kicked him on his private part and escaped outside the house.
She went to the next door neighbour and sat in front of the said house.
Accused came running after her and warned that if she does not cooperate, she should go back in the next train.
When he left, complainant ran into the guest house and locked the main door from inside.
She called her brother Sarthak and another friend by name Dheeraj Mishra and requested them to come to the guest house.
Later complainant and Dheeraj Mishra met the landlord Sri.Keshav at 3.00 a.m. Keshav told her that accused informed him that complainant is his wife.
Accused kept on calling her over phone and repeatedly requested her to meet again.
He offered money and hike in salary.
Even now he is giving threat to her.
Complainant had to walk all the way to the police station with Dheeraj Mishra to file the complaint.

4. Based on the complaint, the concerned police have registered the case in Cr.No.3/2023 and after NC: 2025:KHC:15193 detailed investigation filed charge sheet against the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 354, 376 r/w 511 of I.P.C.
5.
Initially accused was in judicial custody and later secured bail.
6. On committal to the Court of Sessions, accused filed application seeking discharge, which came to be dismissed vide the impugned order.
7. Accused has challenged the same contending that the allegations made in the charge sheet does not attract the provisions of Section 376 I.P.C. Prima facie it is a case of honey trap.
The charge sheet does not indicate the presence of complainant at the spot on the date of alleged offence.
No evidence is collected to show that petitioner traveled from Chattisgarh to Bengaluru.
No CCTV footages are collected.
The allegations made are highly improbable.
There is delay in filing the complaint.
While granting bail, this Court has observed that offence NC: 2025:KHC:15193 under Section 376 is not made out.
There are no eye witnesses to the alleged incident.
Accused is hailing from a highly respectable family.
To make unlawful gain, a false complaint is filed to harass, humiliate and extract money and hence, the petition.

8. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the accused that there is no medical evidence to prove the allegations of rape attracting Section 376 I.P.C and atleast accused is entitled for discharge for Section 376 I.P.C.
9.

On the other hand learned High Court Government Pleader representing the State submitted that complainant was offered the position of Office Assistant by the accused claiming to be the Managing Director of Raj Builders Private Limited.
He went to pick her up from the railway station and made her to stay in a house projecting it as a guest house of the company.
Under the guise of explaining the rules and regulations of the company, he attempted to commit rape on her, which she evaded successfully.
After the incident when complainant ran out of the guest house, he followed her and insisted her to come back.
When she did not agree, he left the place, but called repeatedly offering higher pay package, etc.
When she did not agree, he also gave threat to her.

sentences.text: The allegations against the accused are that he attempted to rape the prosecutrix, but was not successful.
There is prima facie material to proceed against the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 354, 376 r/w Section 511 I.P.C.
Therefore, rightly the trial Court has rejected the application filed by the accused for discharge and pray to reject the present petition also.

10. Heard arguments and perused the record.
11.

From the material placed in the charge sheet, including the complaint averments, it is evident that accused claiming to be the Managing Director of Raj Builders Private Limited offered a job to the complainant in his company.

When she reached Yeshwanthpur railway NC: 2025:KHC:15193 station, though she was told that driver of the company would pick her up, accused himself went to the railway station in his Jaguar car and brought her to a house claiming to be a guest house of the company.
He prevented her from taking her relatives to the guest house and also got rid of her friend who happened to visit her.
11.1 Under the guise of explaining the rules and regulations, he entered the guest house and attempted to commit rape on the prosecutrix.

The details forthcoming from the complaint averments clearly indicate that despite his several attempts to have sexual intercourse with her against her consent, she successfully prevented him and ran out of the guest house.
Even after she left the guest house and sitting outside a negihbouring house, he tried to bring her back luring with higher salary and when it did not work, also gave threat to her.
Even after the incident, he made repeated calls to prevent her from taking any action.
It is not the case of the prosecution that accused succeeded in committing sexual assault on the prosecutrix, but he made persistent attempt to rape her.
Therefore, charge is made against him for the offence punishable under Section 376 r/w Section 511 I.P.C.
Having regard to the nature of the allegations and the circumstances in which the incident took place, it cannot be expected that except the prosecutrix there would any other witness.
At this stage, the statement of the prosecutrix is prima facie sufficient to frame charge against the accused.
Taking into consideration the entire material placed in the charge sheet, the trial Court has rightly rejected the application filed by the accused for discharge.
This Court finds no justifiable grounds to interfere with the impugned order.

In the result, the petition fails and accordingly, the following:
ORDER 1.
Petition filed by the accused under Section 397 r/w 401 Cr.P.C is hereby dismissed.
